title: Thought-Forms
author: Annie Besant and C. W. Leadbeater
description: Thought-Forms by Annie Besant and C. W. Leadbeater (Theosophical Publishing Society, 1901), a classic of Theosophical clairvoyant investigation. Based on an 1896 article in Lucifer, it claims to describe the shapes and colours that thoughts and emotions take in the mental and astral matter of the subtle planes, as perceived by the authors' clairvoyant sight. After explaining the principles that produce thought-forms (the quality of the thought determines colour, its nature determines form, its definiteness determines clarity of outline), it presents a key to the meanings of colours and a series of colour plates showing forms produced by affection, devotion, intellect, ambition, anger, fear and other states, as well as the forms produced by music by Mendelssohn, Gounod and Wagner. Its images are often cited as an influence on early abstract artists such as Kandinsky, Mondrian and Hilma af Klint.
